etymologies.etymologyHTML: From identic +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: (not comparable) Bearing full likeness by having precisely the same set of characteristics; indistinguishable.

quote.text: By this means as many absolutely identical plates can be produced as may be required, and being hardened they will yield a very large number of prints without any appreciable deterioration.

quote.citation: 1972, James H. Rossell, William Wayne Frasure, Managerial Accounting:
quote.text: For example, assume that 10000 identical chairs were produced through incurring the following costs:...
The zygote soon divides into two identical cells.

definitions.definition: (not comparable) Not different or other; not another or others; not different as regards self; selfsame; numerically identical.

quote.citation: 1837, Charles Dickens, The Pantomime of Life:
quote.text: The best of the joke, too, is, that the very coal-merchant who is loudest in his complaints against the person who defrauded him, is the identical man who sat in the centre of the very front row of the pit last night and laughed the most boisterously at this very same thing,--and not so well done either.

quote.citation: 1911, Arthur William Holland, “Habsburg”, in Encyclopædia Britannica:
quote.text: These men were grandsons of a certain Guntram, who, according to some authorities, is identical with a Count Guntram who flourished during the reign of the emperor Otto the Great, and whose ancestry can be traced back to the time of the Merovingian kings.

quote.citation: 1922, Petronius, Satyricon, translation of original by W. C. Firebaugh:
quote.text: Nor could I myself look upon this man without some emotion, for he seemed to be the identical person who had picked up the ragged tunic in the lonely wood, and, as a matter of fact, he was!

definitions.definition: (not comparable, biology) Of twins, sharing the same genetic code.
(comparable, rare) Approximating or approaching exact equivalence.

quote.citation: 1788, Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, The Federalist, section XLI:
quote.text: The terms of Article 8th are still more identical.

definitions.definition: (usually pluralized, chiefly philosophy) Something which has exactly the same properties as something else.

quote.citation: 2014, Robert S. Woodworth, Donald G. Marquis, Psychology (Psychology Revivals): A Study of Mental Life, page 171:
quote.text: Fraternal twins are boy-girl pairs as often as of the same sex, while identicals are necessarily of the same sex,  […]

definitions.definition: (poetry) A rhyme on the same syllable, such as "leave" and "believe".

quote.citation: 1992, Clarence Hugh Holman, William Harmon, A Handbook to Literature, page 439:
quote.text: The strictest construction of the rule requires complete and unvarying repetition of end-words, but some license is granted in the use of identicals.
